findings.issue_text: [High/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11 — `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` dereferences nil whenever the `embed_category` site_settings row is absent or its value doesn't match a category name (empty result set); since Discourse only materializes site settings when changed from defaults, this crashes `db:migrate` for nearly every existing install and all fresh installs (categories aren't seeded yet at migration time).
[High/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:14-16 — the `category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable and itself does an unguarded `[0]['value']` dereference.

[High/data] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24-26 — old `embeddable_hosts` values are inserted verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization, so entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` are stored as-is and can then never match `lower(host) = uri.host` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, silently breaking embedding for those sites after upgrade; the migration should run values through the model (or replicate the stripping/downcasing).

[Medium/security] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` string-interpolates setting-derived data into SQL; a host value containing `'` breaks the statement or allows arbitrary SQL injection; use `quote`/placeholders.
[Medium/security] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb — `val.split("\n")` doesn't reject blank entries, so junk empty-host rows can be inserted.

[Medium/test_gap] spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb — the only specs assert class ancestry; there is no coverage of create/update/destroy behavior (unknown id, invalid host → error JSON, category defaulting to uncategorized), no test that migration-imported protocol/path-bearing hosts still authorize, and no mixed-case host test.

[Low/bug] app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10-17 — `update` and `destroy` operate on `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without a nil check, causing a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404 for stale/unknown ids (e.g., double-delete from two admin sessions).
[Low/bug] app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb — `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host]` unconditionally, causing a 500 on malformed params.

[Low/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:4-7 — `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a nil `host` (e.g., request missing the `host` key) raises NoMethodError before validations run; invalid input surfaces as a 500 instead of a 422 validation error.

[Low/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:15-16 — `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column while `URI(...).host` preserves case (and `before_validation` never downcases saved hosts), so referers like `http://EvilTrout.com` are wrongly denied even though hostnames are case-insensitive (RFC 3986).

[Low/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — the host format regex `\.[a-z]{2,5}` rejects legitimate hosts with longer gTLDs (.technology, .photography, .museum) and punycode IDN TLDs (xn--…), so admins cannot allowlist valid embeddable sites.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — the new plural `_ids` hydration branch deletes the key and assigns `hydrated || []` with no guard, unlike the singular branch's `if (hydrated)` check; if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for a missing side-load (or the key isn't an array), the model receives an array containing `undefined` and loses the original ids — a core path affecting every model, not just embedding.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:36-38 — after saving with no category selected, the server defaults `category_id` to uncategorized, but the client overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` (undefined), so the row renders a blank category until refresh and a subsequent edit derives a broken categoryId.

[Low/doc_defect] spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb vs spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb — the file contents are swapped: the `:embeddable_host` fabricator is defined in `category_fabricator.rb` while all the `:category` fabricators now live in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`; it works (fabricators load globally) but the filenames no longer match their contents.

[Low/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop the table and all its data if it already exists (e.g., re-running after a partial failure or on an environment where it was created out-of-band); drop the `force` option.

[Low/bug] test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:110-118 with test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:227-229 — the updated 'find embedded' test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender `/fruits/:id` handler ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]`, so the new `colors` assertions ([1,2]) validate fruit 1's payload; the test passes against the wrong record and can't detect id-based find regressions.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:14-16 — the `category_id == 0` fallback is unreachable and itself does an unguarded `[0]['value']` dereference.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, `category_id` is assigned via `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i`. If the `embed_category` site_setting is missing or doesn’t match any category name, `execute(...)` returns no rows, so `[0]` is `nil` and the migration will raise before reaching the `if category_id == 0` fallback. Additionally, the fallback query `execute(...)[0]['value']` is also unguarded and would similarly raise if that setting row is absent. Since `categories.id` can’t be 0, the `category_id == 0` branch is effectively unreachable in normal DB states and does not protect against the real failure mode (no rows).

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` where `h` comes from the persisted `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines). Because `h` is interpolated without quoting/escaping, any host containing a `'` will break the SQL, and a crafted value could inject arbitrary SQL during migration. This is directly verifiable in the diff and should use `quote`/bind params.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb — `val.split("\n")` doesn't reject blank entries, so junk empty-host rows can be inserted.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old SiteSetting value, does `records = val.split("\n")`, and then inserts each `h` via raw SQL without filtering. If the setting contains blank lines or a trailing newline, `split` will yield empty-string entries, and the migration will execute `INSERT ... VALUES ('', ...)`. Because this bypasses the model’s `validates_format_of :host` and the DB column is only `null: false` (empty string is allowed), it can create junk/invalid rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy + save_host defaulting category_id to uncategorized; EmbeddableHost host normalization/authorization; a data migration that imports prior embeddable_hosts values via raw SQL; and changes embed authorization to use EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?). However the added controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert inheritance and do not exercise the new behavior paths (e.g., create/update/destroy responses, invalid host handling via validations/render_json_error, category_id defaulting, edge cases like unknown id). Given these code paths are newly introduced and security-relevant (host allowlist), the lack of meaningful tests is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue beyond generic “add more tests.”

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host, with: /\.[a-z]{2,5}.../i` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2). This hard-limits the TLD portion to 2–5 letters, which will reject valid modern gTLDs like `.technology`/`.photography` and also IDN punycode TLDs like `xn--...` (contains hyphens and can exceed 5 chars). As a result, admins would be unable to save legitimate embeddable hosts, breaking the new allowlist feature for those domains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — the new plural `_ids` hydration branch deletes the key and assigns `hydrated || []` with no guard, unlike the singular branch's `if (hydrated)` check; if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for a missing side-load (or the key isn't an array), the model receives an array containing `undefined` and loses the original ids — a core path affecting every model, not just embedding.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new `_ids` branch always does `obj[k].map(...)`, assigns the resulting array to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, and then unconditionally `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular `_id` branch (which only deletes the key when a hydrated object is found), this will (a) throw if `obj[k]` is not actually an array, and (b) if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for missing sideloaded records, produce an array containing `undefined` entries while also discarding the original `*_ids` list. That behavior change is visible directly in the diff and affects all model hydration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:36-38 — after saving with no category selected, the server defaults `category_id` to uncategorized, but the client overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` (undefined), so the row renders a blank category until refresh and a subsequent edit derives a broken categoryId.

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6` `save()` always sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and then, on success, forces `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`. If no category is selected, `categoryId` can be `null`, while the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly defaults blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. The client then overwrites `host.category` with `findById(null)` (undefined), causing `{{category-badge host.category}}` to render blank and later `edit()` to do `this.get('host.category.id')` which can break when `host.category` is unset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop the table and all its data if it already exists (e.g., re-running after a partial failure or on an environment where it was created out-of-band); drop the `force` option.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` that uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, which can cause unintended data loss in non-standard but plausible situations (e.g., table pre-exists from a failed/partial deploy, manual creation, or re-running migrations). This is a robustness/safety concern grounded in the diff, though under normal one-time migration execution it won’t manifest as a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:110-118 with test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:227-229 — the updated 'find embedded' test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender `/fruits/:id` handler ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]`, so the new `colors` assertions ([1,2]) validate fruit 1's payload; the test passes against the wrong record and can't detect id-based find regressions.

adjudication.rationale: In `test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6`, the updated test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` are `[1,2]`. But in `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6`, the `/fruits/:id` handler ignores `:id` and always returns `const fruit = fruits[0]` (which has `color_ids: [1,2]`). So the test passes while actually exercising fruit 1’s payload, and would not catch regressions in id-based lookup.
